## Summary

Adds a functional deck-builder core (M3D1) to the Qt/QML shell: search a
runtime-supplied card database, build Main/Extra/Side explicitly, and
open/save a `.ydk` - through a small Qt adapter layer over the reviewed,
Qt-free `data/` facades from M3A/M3B/M3C (card database, deck model,
fast search).

**This is not the complete M3 "Deck builder UI" roadmap item, and
`docs/ROADMAP.md` deliberately leaves it unchecked.** No legality, no
automatic Main/Extra classification, no artwork, no legacy sigil search
grammar, no full keyboard/controller parity. See
`docs/architecture/deck-builder-ui.md` §12 and [ADR 0006](docs/adr/0006-deck-builder-qt-adapter-boundary.md).

## Update: second follow-up correction pass (4 commits)

A second round of external review, after the first correction pass's
5 findings were fixed, found two more state-ownership bugs plus a
contract/implementation disagreement - all fixed with regression coverage:

- **Keyboard removal bypassed the screen's own selection contract**:
  `DeckSectionList`'s Delete/Backspace handlers called
  `deckController.removeAt()` directly, skipping the cleanup
  (`clearAllSelection()`) the "Remove selected" button already did -
  leaving stale selection/preview state after a keyboard removal.
  `DeckSectionList` now only emits a presentation-level `removeRequested`
  signal; `DeckBuilderScreen.removeDeckEntry()` is the single owner of
  both the removal and its cleanup, for mouse and keyboard alike.
- **A stale search-result selection could survive a model reset**:
  `SearchResultsModel::refresh()` fully resets on every query change or
  catalog reload, but Qt Quick's `ListView` does not reliably re-fire
  `currentIndexChanged` when a reset replaces the *data* at an unchanged
  index - so a selected result could silently keep showing a stale
  preview after typing a new query or reloading the catalog. Fixed by
  connecting to `SearchResultsModel`'s own (already-existing, previously
  unconnected) `resultsChanged` signal.
- **`CardCatalog::loaded()`'s doc comment and implementation disagreed**:
  documented as "true once at least one file loaded successfully," but
  implemented as `cardCount() > 0` - a legitimately empty but valid `.cdb`
  reported `loaded() == false`. Now tracked explicitly from each load's
  own success, independent of `cardCount`.
- `DeckController::addCard(0, ...)` is now a silent no-op - a small,
  audited guard keeping `data/`'s "code 0 is never a real card" invariant
  true from the public API, even though neither real UI path can trigger
  it today.
- A small robustness audit found two other items (an invalid `Section`
  value crossing the QML boundary; catalog replacement while a *deck*
  entry is selected) already safe by inspection - documented rather than
  given speculative new code.

## Update: third follow-up correction pass (1 commit)

External review found a source-fidelity bug in the actual `CardPreview`:
every monster's stored level/rank/link-rating magnitude was labelled
`"Level"` unconditionally, so an Xyz's Rank and a Link's Link Rating both
displayed as `"Level"`; a Link's DEF rendered as `"<ATK> / LINK"` text with
no rating anywhere in it; and although `CardEntry` already carried
`linkMarker`, nothing ever rendered it.

Fixed entirely in the Qt adapter/QML presentation seam, cited directly
against `Game::ShowCardInfo` (`gframe/game.cpp`) and
`DataManager::FormatLinkMarker` (`gframe/data_manager.cpp`) as the source
of truth - `data/`'s `CardRecord` needed no changes, it already carries
`type`/`level`/`link_marker` faithfully:

- `CardEntry` gains `isXyz` and `linkMarkerDisplay`, following the existing
  verified-bit precedent `isMonster`/`isLink`/`isPendulum` already
  established.
- `CardPreview.qml`'s monster grid is now independent ATK / DEF /
  Level-or-Rank-or-Link-Rating / Link Markers rows instead of the old
  universal `"ATK / DEF"` + `"Level"` pair. DEF is hidden (not shown as a
  fake `0`) for a Link; the shared magnitude row is labelled `"Level"`,
  `"Rank"`, or `"Link Rating"` by `isXyz`/`isLink`; link markers render via
  `linkMarkerDisplay`, in upstream's own fixed positional order.
- New regression coverage at both layers:
  `ordinaryMonsterEntryIsNotClassifiedAsXyzOrLink`,
  `xyzMonsterEntryIsClassifiedAsXyzNotLink`,
  `linkMonsterEntryHasNoRealDefenseAndFormatsItsMarkers`
  (`test_deckbuilder.cpp`, adapter-level) and
  `ordinaryMonsterPreviewLabelsItsLevelCorrectly`,
  `xyzMonsterPreviewLabelsItsRankNotLevel`,
  `linkMonsterPreviewHidesDefenseAndShowsLinkRatingAndMarkers`
  (`test_deckbuilder_screen.cpp`, asserting the actual rendered `Text`
  items in the real `CardPreview.qml`).
- `docs/architecture/deck-builder-ui.md` §10.7 documents the fix.

Test count at this point: 18 functions in `test_deckbuilder.cpp` + 17 in
`test_deckbuilder_screen.cpp` = 35, across 2 CTest targets, all passing.

## Update: fourth follow-up correction pass (1 commit)

A fresh Codex review of the third pass's own commit (`281e908c`) found one more
instance of the same underlying mistake, one field over: `CardRecord::attack`/
`defense` document `-1`/`-2` as real, displayed "varies" values, and upstream's
`Game::ShowCardInfo` (`gframe/game.cpp`) renders any negative value as literal
`"?"` - `CardPreview.qml` and `SearchResultsModel::build_summary()` were both
printing the raw negative number instead (e.g. `"ATK -2 / DEF -1"`).

Fixed the same way as the third pass: `CardEntry` gains `attackDisplay`/
`defenseDisplay`, computed once by a tiny formatter matching upstream's `< 0`
check exactly (not a narrower `== -1`/`== -2` equality test).
`CardPreview.qml`'s ATK/DEF rows and the search summary line both read these
instead of the raw numbers, so the two presentations share one computation.
`attack`/`defense` themselves are untouched.

New coverage: `negativeCombatStatsRenderAsQuestionMarks` (also confirms an
ordinary positive-stat card is unaffected) and
`searchSummaryRendersUnknownCombatStatsAsQuestionMarks` (`test_deckbuilder.cpp`),
`negativeCombatStatsRenderAsQuestionMarksInPreview` against the real rendered
`CardPreview.qml` (`test_deckbuilder_screen.cpp`).
`docs/architecture/deck-builder-ui.md` §10.8 documents the fix.

Final test count: **20 functions in `test_deckbuilder.cpp` + 18 in
`test_deckbuilder_screen.cpp` = 38, across 2 CTest targets**, all passing.
